title: Exponential and logarithmic equations and a single logarithm
intro: No calculator. Give exact values and show the work that leads to each answer.

rubric.point: $x = \frac{1 + \ln 7}{3}$, with the power isolated before taking $\ln$

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.sample: Product property: $\log_2(x(x + 6)) = 4$, so $x^2 + 6x = 16$ and $(x + 8)(x - 2) = 0$. $x = -8$ makes $\log_2 x$ undefined, so it is extraneous. The solution is $x = 2$.

parts.label: B(i)
parts.prompt: Rewrite $2\ln(x + 1) - \ln x + 3\ln 2$ as a single natural logarithm, for $x > 0$.
parts.sample: Power property: $\ln(x + 1)^2 - \ln x + \ln 8$. Product and quotient: $\ln \frac{8(x + 1)^2}{x}$.

parts.label: B(ii)
parts.prompt: Rewrite $9^x \cdot 3^{2 - x}$ as a single power of $3$.

parts.label: C
parts.sample: $-\log_2(x + 1) \ge -2$, so $\log_2(x + 1) \le 2$. Since $\log_2$ is increasing, $x + 1 \le 4$, so $x \le 3$. The logarithm also needs $x + 1 > 0$, so $x > -1$. The solution is $-1 < x \le 3$.
